question: What is the Principle of Double Effect, and what are its four conditions?

choices.A: An act with both good and bad effects may be permissible if: (1) the act itself is not evil; (2) the agent intends only the good effect; (3) the bad effect is not the means to the good; (4) there is proportionate reason
choices.B: If a doctor performs two operations in sequence, both outcomes count as equally intended
choices.C: Any act with both a good and bad effect is forbidden, regardless of intention
choices.D: The good effects of an act always outweigh the bad if the person is acting in good faith

teaching.title: Principle of Double Effect
teaching.body: The Principle of Double Effect (PDE), classically attributed to Thomas Aquinas (Summa II-II, q.64, a.7 on self-defense), addresses acts whose effects include both good and harmful outcomes. The four conditions for permissibility: (1) The act itself must not be intrinsically evil; (2) The agent must intend the good effect, not the harmful one (though the latter is foreseen); (3) The harmful effect must not be the means by which the good is achieved; (4) There must be proportionate reason — the good must outweigh or at least balance the harm. Classic application: a surgeon removing a cancerous uterus containing a fetus — the death of the fetus is foreseen but not intended.
refs: Grisez, The Way of the Lord Jesus
